transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Gupta (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (OmniChain Head of Search), Ben Torres (Infra), Hannah Li (ML)

Summary:
Short scoping call to align on a POC for embeddings + rerank. Customer wants a pilot for a high-QPS omnichannel search layer (web + mobile + vector fanout to on-prem DBs). Discussion covered embedding dims, hybrid top-k vs rerank, hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), throughput targets, and what datasets and traces OmniChain will provide. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Target QPS and tail latency SLOs
- Embedding dimensionality (512 / 768 / 1024 tradeoffs)
- Vector DB integration and fallback topology
- Private deployment / VPC constraints and audit logs
- Benchmark harness and sample corpus

Action items (captured above): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Maya who is our SE will walk through throughput stuff. Priya, Ben, Hannah, thanks for making time. quick agenda — align on POC scope, SLOs, data sharing, and next steps.

[01:10] Priya Nair: Hi, yeah thanks. To set context, OmniChain's search is multi-tenant across 3 products, we currently fan out to an on-prem Postgres and an internal similarity store. We're evaluating moving embeddings into a centralized vector tier with rerank so we can push more semantic relevance across channels. 

[02:05] Maya Gupta: Great, thanks Priya. Couple clarifying q's up front — what's the expected QPS at peak and what's an acceptable 95/99 latency? That'll drive whether Hosted can meet it or we need Dedicated/Private.

[02:40] Ben Torres: We're seeing averages around 120 QPS right now, but spikes to 800 QPS during release windows. Our 95th needs to be sub 200ms for the web search path, 99th ideally sub 500ms. Mobile can tolerate a bit more. 

[03:10] Hannah Li: On the ML side, we're testing 1024-dim embeddings derived from our internal transformer. But we've seen decent recall with 512 dims if we use reranking on the top 50. Concern is storage and throughput cost with 1024.

[03:55] Alex Chen: That's a classic tradeoff — dims vs recall vs latency. For the POC we often prototype with 768 dims as a middle ground; gives better vector quality than 512 for many models but reduced storage vs 1024. But if your model is 1024 natively, we can do quantization/FP16 or int8 to reduce footprint.

[04:40] Priya Nair: What about the hybrid search setup — we want to do ANN + sub-second rerank using a lightweight cross-encoder. Can Redwood host the cross-encoder or do we need to host that ourselves?

[05:10] Maya Gupta: We can run the cross-encoder inside Redwood Hosted for prototype, or inside Dedicated pools if you need predictability. For Private/VPC, you can run the model in your VPC with our private control plane, and we support model routing so the initial ANN search can hit your vector DB and the rerank calls go to a Redwood-internal runtime or optionally a customer-hosted endpoint. There are latency tradeoffs when the rerank is a remote (over-VPC) call.

[06:05] Ben Torres: If rerank goes over VPC to us, we worry about extra hops and tail. We are leaning to keep rerank inside Redwood if possible, but data residency and SOC2 are concerns.

[06:30] Alex Chen: Understood. Redwood Private (VPC) is designed to address that — you keep data in your network, we provide the runtime images and orchestration. SOC 2 reports and audit logs are available; we can redline contract clauses if needed.

[07:05] Priya Nair: How do you handle vector DB integration? We run a sharded Milvus cluster on-prem and also push a subset into a cloud index for web queries. We want fallback if cloud index lag occurs.

[07:45] Maya Gupta: We commonly integrate via your vector DB connector, or via a sync to a hosted index. Our routing policies support fanout + fallback: query to local Milvus first, if latency exceeds threshold we fallback to a hosted index (or a lower-dim approx). We can also do top-k hybrid: ANN top 200, then rerank top 50. For sharded DBs, we recommend parallel fetches with async KV cache to reduce repeated work.

[08:50] Hannah Li: Could you explain the KV cache — I saw that in the docs but not sure how it would work for a multi-tenant fanout.

[09:10] Maya Gupta: Yeah, KV cache holds per-request key/value decoder states for recent prefixes; helps token generation paths, less relevant for pure embed+search. For rerank we use result-level caching — if identical queries surface the same top-K, we can cache the rerank outputs or precompute rerank scores for known heavy queries. It reduces cost and latency for hot queries.

[10:15] Priya Nair: For the POC we want to validate quality lift from rerank plus confirm we can hit 800 QPS bursts. What's a typical setup you recommend for the pilot?

[10:45] Alex Chen: Pilot pattern we do: 1) run a small-run hosted prototype with 20k sample docs to validate quality and rerank uplift, 2) run a dedicated benchmark on a dedicated pool sized for your 95/99 targets using your 1TB sample corpus and real QPS trace, and 3) iterate on dims/quantization. We'll provide a benchmark harness so you can reproduce.

[11:30] Ben Torres: For step 2, what does dedicated sizing look like? GPUs? number of workers?

[11:50] Maya Gupta: Depends on model size for rerank, and vector index throughput. Example: if rerank uses a small cross-encoder (100M–300M params) you can run many requests per GPU with batching; for 800 peak QPS with 99th under 500ms we often suggest 2 pooled GPUs with autoscaling to 4 for burst. Vector index throughput is often the bottleneck — we'll recommend sharding and having local vector workers close to the dataset. We'll share an initial sizing sheet.

[12:45] Priya Nair: Do you support quantized models for rerank? We tried int8 and saw some drop but 1-2% recall delta might be acceptable.

[13:05] Maya Gupta: Yes, we support int8 and 4-bit quant formats depending on model family. We can run a quantization sensitivity test in the POC to measure recall impact. Often quantization plus post-training calibration yields minimal production impact.

[14:00] Hannah Li: Any gotchas with vector dimension mismatch between stored vectors and the embedding model we use?

[14:25] Alex Chen: If your stored vectors are 1024 and you change to 768, you'd need to reindex or maintain parallel indexes. Redwood can help with migration strategies: dual-indexing during transition, or on-the-fly projection in some cases but that's typically approximate. For the POC we recommend sticking with your native embedding dim.

[15:00] Priya Nair: For monitoring and observability we need per-query traces, token-level cost breakdown isn't relevant but per-route latency and rerank failure rates are. Can Console surface that?

[15:20] Maya Gupta: Yes — Redwood Console has per-route latency, per-model tail latency, rerank success/failure, and cost by token. We can also attach tracing hooks to your APM and export audit logs.

[16:05] Ben Torres: Security - we need SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration and logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also encryption of embeddings at rest.

[16:30] Alex Chen: Those are standard. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported, KMS integrations for Private deployments and encryption at rest are in our feature list. We'll attach compliance docs + SOC 2.

[17:05] Priya Nair: Real quick — cost. Are you able to ballpark what the delta is between hosted and dedicated for our expected load?

[17:25] Alex Chen: Ballpark only: hosted is usually higher per-token but lower ops overhead. Dedicated is better when you have predictable peak and want lower unit costs. I'll send a pricing worksheet with two example scenarios (hosted bursty, dedicated steady) so you can compare.

[18:10] Hannah Li: For the vector DB sync — would Redwood manage delta syncs or do you expect us to run a pipeline?

[18:30] Maya Gupta: We have connectors and a recommended sync pattern — you can push data to a hosted index or we can run a connector that streams inserts/updates. For on-prem Milvus, many customers run a small sync agent that ships deltas; we can provide the connector code and ops playbook.

[19:15] Priya Nair: Let's talk evaluation metrics for the POC. We care about improvement in NDCG@10, latency P95/P99, and cost per query. We'll provide baseline metrics for the current system.

[19:45] Alex Chen: Perfect. Our eval harness will measure NDCG/Recall, and we'll add synthetic QPS tests to capture tail latency. We'll correlate model configs with unit cost.

[20:30] Ben Torres: On the infra timeline — if we agreed, how quickly could we have a dedicated pool ready for benchmark runs?

[20:50] Maya Gupta: If you sign a pilot reserved commitment, we can provision dedicated pool within 2–3 weeks. For Hosted prototype it's immediate. Private/VPC takes longer because we need network setup — usually 3–5 weeks depending on firewall and cert work.

[21:30] Priya Nair: For the POC scope let's outline success criteria — 10%+ NDCG uplift vs baseline, P95 < 200ms for web path under typical load, and cost per query within 1.5x current. Are those reasonable?

[21:55] Alex Chen: Yes those are actionable. We'll encode them in the POC charter.

[22:20] Hannah Li: A few nitty-gritty questions — do you support rerank batching to amortize cost? Also, how do you handle cold starts for models in dedicated pools?

[22:45] Maya Gupta: Rerank batching is supported; we have continuous batching in the runtime — but beware of latency tradeoffs since batching increases per-request latency. For cold starts we keep warm pools and have fast model swap; Dedicated pools maintain pinned model residency to avoid cold starts for production configs.

[23:40] Ben Torres: If we do a hybrid approach, where ANN index is on-prem and rerank hosted, are there SLA implications?

[24:00] Alex Chen: Yes — hybrid cross-network calls add failure modes. We usually recommend keeping the critical low-latency path co-located. If that's not possible, add fallback policies: if on-prem index is slow, fall back to a hosted index with slightly lower recall.

[25:00] Priya Nair: Could we run a short throughput benchmark now — at least rough numbers during the call — to see if the numbers line up?

[25:20] Maya Gupta: We can do a quick sanity run using our internal bench, but we need your exact model and corpus for apples-to-apples. I can run a synthetic run that simulates 768-dim vectors and a cross-encoder rerank pattern. Would that help?

[25:55] Priya Nair: Yes, run the synthetic for now just to validate the ceiling. We'll share the real traces later.

[26:20] Maya Gupta: Ok I'll spin up a quick sim and report back over email. Expected synthetic: on a 2-GPU dedicated pool simulated rerank (small cross-encoder) you can expect 600–900 QPS depending on batching and index topology. That lines with your burst needs.

[27:10] Hannah Li: What about cold query patterns — if you have long tail queries that produce unique rerank inputs, caching won't help and costs could spike. Any recommendations?

[27:35] Alex Chen: For long tail, use a tiered approach: hot queries served from cached rerank or precomputed candidates, warm queries get fast ANN+light rerank, cold queries can be queued or served at slightly higher latency. Also consider augmenting with query rewriting to increase overlap.

[28:20] Priya Nair: Onboarding — who will be our SE contact during the pilot?

[28:35] Alex Chen: Maya will lead the technical side. I'll coordinate commercial. We'll also assign an engineer for infra setup during the dedicated/provisioning step.

[29:00] Ben Torres: For the POC dataset we'll likely send you a 1TB sample and a day-by-day QPS trace including peak windows. Any format preference?

[29:20] Maya Gupta: Parquet or JSONL for embeddings and traces is great. Schema: id, embedding vector (list), metadata fields, timestamp. For queries, just a CSV with timestamp, query text, user-agent, route.

[30:05] Priya Nair: Is there any possibility to do partial indexing — like keep 70% of vectors in-memory and the rest on SSD for cost savings?

[30:25] Maya Gupta: Yes, tiered indices are possible: hot in-memory shards and cold SSD-backed shards. Our runtime supports routing to preferred tiers based on TTL or frequency heuristics. That can reduce cost but adds complexity in routing.

[31:10] Hannah Li: We saw some mention in docs about quantization-aware indexing. How mature is that?

[31:30] Maya Gupta: It's pretty mature for common models — we support quantized indexes for ANN search. We recommend running sensitivity tests on your embeddings. We'll help instrument that as part of the POC.

[32:00] Alex Chen: Quick commercial note — pilot agreement will outline data handling, a small reserved commit for dedicated if you choose that path, and a timeline. We can share a draft within 48 hours.

[32:30] Priya Nair: Good. Also, we might evaluate Weaviate as a lightweight alternative later; just flagging that for procurement.

[32:50] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll include a competitor matrix in the materials.

[33:20] Ben Torres: One more thing — for the private deployment, can we run the entire stack on-prem including orchestration?

[33:40] Maya Gupta: We offer an on-prem package where the customer controls the runtime and we provide an offline control plane that can be air-gapped. It requires a short integration window for certs and ops handoff.

[34:15] Priya Nair: Okay, sounds good. Let's nail down timeline: we aim to have pilot kickoff week of 2027-02-22, with initial hosted prototype within a week of kickoff and dedicated benchmark in two weeks after kickoff.

[34:45] Alex Chen: That timeline is feasible. We'll send a calendar invite for kickoff.

[35:10] Hannah Li: For evaluation tooling, can you push sample dashboards to our grafana or only to Redwood Console?

[35:30] Maya Gupta: We can export metrics to your monitoring via Prometheus/Grafana integrations and also provide the Console dashboards.

[36:05] Priya Nair: Ok community question — do you do A/B rollouts for model changes? We need safe rollouts for rerank model updates.

[36:25] Maya Gupta: Yes, Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts at route or token-level, automatic rollback on metric regressions, and staged traffic percentages.

[37:00] Ben Torres: Any concern about GDPR/data residency with embeddings? We might have EU users and need to keep those vectors in-region.

[37:25] Alex Chen: We support regional hosting and can pin data to EU regions. For Private deployments, you can keep everything in your EU cluster. We'll surface data residency in the contract.

[38:00] Priya Nair: Great. A few quick clarifications on the POC deliverables?

[38:20] Alex Chen: Deliverables: 1) Hosted prototype results (quality uplift, baseline comparison) 2) Dedicated benchmark report (latency, throughput, cost) 3) Migration/ops playbook (sync connector, indexing steps) 4) POC retro and recommendation.

[38:50] Priya Nair: Sounds good. If we meet the success criteria we'll consider expanding to a reserved contract.

[39:10] Hannah Li: One last technical — do you have built-in rerank baselines (e.g., monoT5 variants) or do we bring our model?

[39:30] Maya Gupta: We can provide baseline rerank models (small cross-encoder / monoT5 style) for comparison. You're welcome to bring your own model and we'll host it.

[40:05] Ben Torres: Are there any quotas or limits on the hosted trial?

[40:20] Alex Chen: For the initial hosted prototype we'll give a small credit and a soft quota; for larger loads we move to dedicated pilot with committed capacity.

[40:50] Priya Nair: Ok I think we've covered most things. Can you repeat the artifacts you'll send?

[41:05] Alex Chen: Sure — (1) pricing worksheet (hosted vs dedicated vs private), (2) benchmark harness and runbook, (3) compliance pack (SOC2 + data handling), (4) POC charter template. We'll send those within 48 hours.

[41:40] Priya Nair: And the data format we agreed is Parquet JSONL and a CSV trace. We'll aim to deliver by Feb 17.

[42:00] Alex Chen: Great. Any other open questions?

[42:10] Hannah Li: One micro ask — can you include recommended embedding dim experiments? Like 512 vs 768 vs 1024 with suggested sample sizes?

[42:30] Maya Gupta: Yes we'll include a recommended matrix and sample sizes for statistical significance.

[43:00] Priya Nair: Good. Last thing — procurement will ask for references. Can we get a list of similar customers?

[43:20] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include anonymized references that did embedding+rerank pilots.

[43:50] Ben Torres: Sounds good. Ready to wrap.

[44:05] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, quick recap in chat: Alex sends pricing and POC draft; Maya sends bench harness; OmniChain to send dataset and traces by Feb 17; Kickoff week of Feb 22. We'll follow up with calendar invite and attach docs.

[45:00] Priya Nair: Thanks, appreciate it.

[45:10] Hannah Li: Thanks all.

[45:20] Maya Gupta: Thanks, bye.

[45:25] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cache", "Redwood Optima" mis-hear), filler words kept to preserve authenticity.
